question:
(a) Compare infrared rays, ultraviolet rays and X-rays on the basis of their relative frequency, wavelength, source and one use each.
(b) Which among them has the greatest penetrating power and why?

options.A:
Infrared rays: Lowest frequency and longest wavelength among the three; emitted by hot bodies and molecules; used in remote controls or thermal imaging.
Ultraviolet rays: Higher frequency and shorter wavelength than visible light; produced by very hot bodies and special lamps; used for sterilisation.
X-rays: Higher frequency and shorter wavelength than ultraviolet rays; produced when high-energy electrons are suddenly stopped by a metal target; used in medical diagnosis or crystal studies.
Greatest penetrating power: X-rays, because their higher frequency gives higher photon energy $(E=h\\nu)$.
options.B:
Infrared rays: Highest frequency and shortest wavelength; produced in nuclear reactions; used for cancer treatment.
Ultraviolet rays: Lower frequency than infrared; produced by hot bodies; used in remote controls.
X-rays: Lowest frequency; produced by special lamps; used for sterilisation.
Greatest penetrating power: Infrared rays because they have the longest wavelength.
options.C:
Infrared rays: Produced by hot bodies; used for thermal imaging.
Ultraviolet rays: Produced by lamps; used for sterilisation.
X-rays: Produced by electrons striking a target; used for diagnosis.
Relative order: X-rays have the longest wavelength and infrared rays the shortest.
Greatest penetrating power: Ultraviolet rays because their wavelength is longest.
options.D:
Infrared rays: Lower frequency than visible light; emitted by hot bodies; used in remote controls.
Ultraviolet rays: Higher frequency than visible light; produced by hot bodies and lamps; used for sterilisation.
X-rays: Higher frequency than ultraviolet rays; produced by electrons stopped at a metal target; used in diagnosis.
Greatest penetrating power: Infrared rays because photon energy decreases with frequency.
